items.title: Finite-volume families with a regular simplicial companion

references.title: Jérôme Droniou, Finite volume schemes for diffusion equations: introduction to and review of modern methods, 2014
references.locator: Complete 38-page PDF retrieved and extracted; inspected section 1.2 and sections 4–4.1. The explicit companion construction and parabolic proof are supplied locally.

items.statement:
Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a nonempty bounded connected Lipschitz polyhedral domain, $d\ge1$. A **regular simplicial companion family** consists of refining uniformly regular boundary-anchored cell-face meshes in [[def-fv-admissible-cell-face-mesh]], and, for each mesh, a matching simplicial subdivision $\mathcal S_h$ of its cells with the following finite geometric data and uniform constants $c,C,J>0$.

Each cell is subdivided into at most $J$ closed nondegenerate $d$-simplices. Each simplex has diameter at most $Ch$ and inradius at least $ch$, and the chosen cell point $x_K$ is a subdivision vertex. The subdivision of each cell is a fan from $x_K$ over a triangulation of its boundary, and subdivisions agree on shared faces. Each original face is a union of at most $J$ subdivision facets. In dimension one these mean the two subintervals from $x_K$ to the endpoints.

For each subdivision vertex $z$, let $\mathcal K(z)$ consist of the original cells whose closures contain $z$. This set has at most $J$ elements. For any $K,L\in\mathcal K(z)$ there is a path of at most $J$ cells in $\mathcal K(z)$, from $K$ to $L$, consecutive cells sharing an original face whose closure contains $z$. If $z\in\partial\Omega$, every $K\in\mathcal K(z)$ has such a path to a cell with a boundary face whose closure contains $z$. These are connectivity checks on finite vertex stars, not an assumption of an analytic inequality.

For shared face values $v_F$, cell values $v_K$, and homogeneous boundary values $v_F=0$, define the piecewise constant state $\Pi_hv|_K=v_K$ and
$$D_{h,p}(v)^p=\sum_K\sum_{F\subset\partial K}|F|d_{K,F}^{1-p}|v_F-v_K|^p\qquad(1<p<\infty).$$
The mean interpolator $I_hv$ has cell and face values equal to the corresponding means of a Sobolev function, with face means interpreted by the simplex trace; for $v\in W_0^{1,p}(\Omega)$ its boundary face means are zero. Define $E_hv$ to be continuous and affine on each subdivision simplex, with nodal value $|\mathcal K(z)|^{-1}\sum_{K\in\mathcal K(z)}v_K$ at an interior vertex $z$ and zero at a boundary vertex. Thus $E_h$ is an explicit linear function of the cell values; its definition does not assume its stability.

These conditions allow nonorthogonal cells. A nonempty example in every dimension is the uniform cubical partition of $(0,1)^d$, with cell centers, a fixed matching barycentric subdivision of every face, and the cones from cell centers to those face simplices. Scaling leaves finitely many simplex shapes and bounded vertex stars; coordinate adjacency connects each interior star and connects each boundary star to a boundary face. In dimension one use equal subintervals and their midpoints. Hence all the displayed constants can be chosen independently of refinement.

items.title: TPFA discrete Green identity, coercivity, and maximum principle
items.statement: On a finite connected orthogonal mesh whose cell graph is anchored to Dirichlet boundary faces, shared TPFA fluxes are locally conservative, the cell matrix is symmetric positive definite in the transmissibility energy, and nonnegative source and boundary data give nonnegative cell values.
items.strategy: Pair the cell balance with a test vector, collect the two signed contributions at each interior face, and use positivity plus boundary anchoring for injectivity and the minimum argument.
items.axiom_base: No choice axiom is used; the graph and all sums are finite.

items.title: Discrete Poincaré inequality from boundary paths
items.statement: For a finite TPFA mesh supplied with cell-to-boundary paths and a finite congestion constant, the piecewise-constant cell reconstruction satisfies an explicit discrete Poincaré inequality in the transmissibility energy norm.
items.strategy: Write each cell value as the signed sum of its path increments, apply weighted Cauchy–Schwarz, and exchange the finite cell-edge sums using the stated congestion bound.
items.axiom_base: No choice axiom is used; the paths are finite data and all sums are finite.

items.title: Coercivity, monotonicity, conservation, and affine exactness of the mimetic schemes
items.statement: The symmetric linear hybrid mimetic method is locally coercive, globally positive definite under boundary anchoring, locally conservative, and affine-exact for cellwise-constant SPD tensors; its p-growth backward-Euler extension is monotone, coercive, and conservatively balanced.
items.strategy: Use the divergence theorem to prove affine gradient reproduction, then use the residual stabilization and constant-vector kernel to prove coercivity, global uniqueness, and face balance.
items.axiom_base: No choice axiom is used; all spaces are finite-dimensional.

items.title: Finite-volume companions, mean tests and weak-gradient closure

references.title: Jérôme Droniou, Finite volume schemes for diffusion equations: introduction to and review of modern methods, 2014
references.locator: Complete 38-page PDF retrieved and extracted; inspected section 1.2 and sections 4–4.1. The explicit companion construction and parabolic proof are supplied locally.

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and a family in [[def-fv-regular-simplicial-companion-family]]. For $1<p<\infty$ and zero boundary face values, put
$$B_{h,p}(v)^p=\sum_K|K||G_Kv|^p+S_{h,p}(v)^p,\qquad S_{h,p}(v)^p=\sum_{K,F}|F|d_{K,F}^{1-p}|\rho_{K,F}(v)|^p,$$
where $G_K,\rho_{K,F}$ have the formulas in [[def-hybrid-mimetic-fv-scheme]]. Then, with constants independent of $h,v$,
$$C^{-1}D_{h,p}(v)\le B_{h,p}(v)\le CD_{h,p}(v),\quad \|E_hv\|_{W^{1,p}}\le CD_{h,p}(v),\quad \|\Pi_hv-E_hv\|_{L^p}\le ChD_{h,p}(v).$$
Here $E_hv\in W_0^{1,p}(\Omega)$. If $p>\max(1,2d/(d+2))$ and $\vartheta=1-d\max(1/p-1/2,0)>0$, also
$$\|\Pi_hv-E_hv\|_2\le Ch^\vartheta D_{h,p}(v),\qquad \|\Pi_hv\|_2+\|\Pi_hv\|_p\le CD_{h,p}(v).$$
For $z\in W_0^{1,p}(\Omega)$, $D_{h,p}(I_hz)\le C\|\nabla z\|_p$. If the cell points are volume centroids, then for smooth $z$ with compact support in $\Omega$, $G_h I_hz\to\nabla z$ uniformly and $S_{h,p}(I_hz)\le Ch\|D^2z\|_\infty$, where $G_hv|_K=G_Kv$. Finally, for every smooth vector field $\phi$ on a neighborhood of $\overline\Omega$,
$$\left|\int_\Omega G_hv\cdot\phi+\Pi_hv\,\operatorname{div}\phi\right|\le ChD_{h,p}(v)\|\nabla\phi\|_\infty.$$
Consequently bounded $D_{h,p}(v_h)$, strong $L^p$ convergence $\Pi_hv_h\to v$, and weak $L^p$ convergence $G_hv_h\rightharpoonup g$ imply $g=\nabla v$ distributionally. The same statements hold after integration in time with the corresponding $L^p$ bounds.

items.title: TPFA flux-energy convergence for smooth face-aligned interfaces
items.statement: For a regular orthogonal mesh family and a cellwise-constant positive isotropic coefficient with jumps aligned to faces, a piecewise C2 solution with conservative face-integrated flux has TPFA numerical face fluxes converging to the exact face-integrated flux in the transmissibility-dual energy norm at rate O(h).
items.strategy: Use the common face-average exact flux, bound each cell normal trace deviation by the Hessian bound, and use normal Taylor expansion and conservative energy testing.
items.axiom_base: No choice axiom is used; the proof uses finite sums and Taylor's theorem.

items.title: Discrete TPFA Rellich compactness and physical weak gradients

references.title: Jérôme Droniou, Finite volume schemes for diffusion equations: introduction to and review of modern methods, 2014
references.locator: Complete 38-page PDF retrieved and extracted; inspected section 1.2 and sections 4–4.1. The explicit companion construction and parabolic proof are supplied locally.

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let TPFA-admissible meshes also form a regular simplicial companion family, with homogeneous Dirichlet data and fixed $0<\lambda_*\le\lambda_K\le\lambda^*$. If cell vectors $v_h$ satisfy $\sup_h\|v_h\|_{E_h}<\infty$, there are a subsequence and $v\in H_0^1(\Omega)$ such that $\Pi_hv_h\to v$ strongly in $L^2(\Omega)$, and the gradients of the conforming companions converge weakly to $\nabla v$ in $L^2$.

There is also an explicit physical weak-gradient reconstruction. Let $P_{K,F}$ be the pyramid with vertex $x_K$ and base $\overline F$, ignoring its measure-zero boundary. For $F=K|L$ put $\mathcal D_F=P_{K,F}\cup P_{L,F}$, fix the normal $n=n_{K,F}$, and define
$$\mathcal G_hv=d\frac{v_L-v_K}{d_F}n\quad\hbox{on }\mathcal D_F.$$
On a boundary pyramid put $\mathcal G_hv=-dv_Kn_{K,F}/d_{K,F}$. These regions partition $\Omega$ up to null sets. Along the same subsequence $\mathcal G_hv_h\rightharpoonup\nabla v$ in $L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^d)$, and
$$\|\mathcal G_hv_h\|_2^2=d\left(\sum_{F=K|L}\frac{|F|}{d_F}|v_L-v_K|^2+\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_{\rm bdy}}\frac{|F|}{d_{K,F}}|v_K|^2\right)\le\frac d{\lambda_*}\|v_h\|_{E_h}^2.$$
The dimension factor $d$ is essential. This physical gradient differs from the face-copy bookkeeping gradient in the TPFA Definition; no identification of that separate copy space with $\Omega$ is asserted.

items.title: Conditional monotone finite-volume parabolic limit identification
items.statement: On the stated bounded open C1 domain and under the exact exponent/data hypotheses, if finite-volume state reconstructions admit conforming Sobolev reconstructions with the PE12 strong-state and weak-gradient limits, their discrete weak equations converge, and their energies satisfy the Minty limsup bound, then every such limit solves the parabolic equation with the correct monotone flux graph.
items.strategy: Apply PE12 weak compactness to the assumed conforming reconstructions, pass the discrete weak identity under the stated residual hypothesis, and apply Minty's lemma using the discrete energy limsup.
items.axiom_base: Assume the Axiom of Choice. It is used only by the PE12 weak-gradient compactness and Minty supplier chain; no additional choice is used in the finite-volume balance passage.

items.title: Energy and computed-state compactness for hybrid mimetic backward Euler

references.title: Jérôme Droniou, Finite volume schemes for diffusion equations: introduction to and review of modern methods, 2014
references.locator: Complete 38-page PDF retrieved and extracted; inspected section 1.2 and sections 4–4.1. The explicit companion construction and parabolic proof are supplied locally.

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let hybrid meshes in [[def-hybrid-mimetic-fv-scheme]] form a regular simplicial companion family, with cell points equal to volume centroids, and let $0<\underline\alpha\le\alpha_{0,K}\le\overline\alpha<\infty$ uniformly. Let $p>\max(1,2d/(d+2))$, $p'=p/(p-1)$, and let $a$ have precisely the Carathéodory, growth, coercivity and monotonicity hypotheses of [[def-pe12-monotone-diffusion-flux]]. Let $f\in L^{p'}(Q)$, $Q=(0,T)\times\Omega$, and let initial cell states obey $\Pi_hU_h^0\to u_0$ strongly in $H=L^2(\Omega)$. Each finite backward-Euler step in the hybrid Definition has a solution. Initial face values can be set arbitrarily because only initial cell values occur in the time term.

On arbitrary time partitions with maximum step $\delta_h\to0$, every selection of step solutions satisfies, uniformly in $h$,
$$\max_n\|\Pi_hU_h^n\|_2^2+\sum_n\|\Pi_h(U_h^n-U_h^{n-1})\|_2^2+\sum_n\tau_n B_{h,p}(U_h^n)^p\le C.$$
Here $B_{h,p},D_{h,p},S_{h,p},G_h$ are as in [[lem-fv-conforming-companion-and-test-recovery]]. Extend $\overline U_h$ by $U_h^n$ on $(t_{n-1},t_n]$. The piecewise affine interpolation of $\Pi_hU_h^n$ has derivative bounded in $L^{p'}(0,T;V^*)$, $V=W_0^{1,p}(\Omega)$. There are a subsequence and $u\in L^p(0,T;V)\cap L^\infty(0,T;H)$ such that
$$\Pi_h\overline U_h\to u\text{ in }L^r(0,T;H)\ (1\le r<\infty)\text{ and in }L^p(Q),$$
$$E_h\overline U_h\rightharpoonup u\text{ in }L^p(0,T;V),\qquad G_h\overline U_h\rightharpoonup\nabla u\text{ in }L^p(Q;\mathbb R^d).$$
No mesh/time coupling or time-step ratio restriction is required.

items.title: Computed hybrid mimetic states and numerical fluxes converge to monotone diffusion

references.title: Jérôme Droniou, Finite volume schemes for diffusion equations: introduction to and review of modern methods, 2014
references.locator: Complete 38-page PDF retrieved and extracted; inspected section 1.2 and sections 4–4.1. The explicit companion construction and parabolic proof are supplied locally.

items.statement:
Under exactly the hypotheses of [[lem-hybrid-mimetic-backward-euler-energy-and-compactness]], the computed cell states converge, along a subsequence, to a weak evolution solution $u$ of $u_t-\operatorname{div}(a(x,\nabla u))=f$, $u(0)=u_0$, in the sense of [[def-pe12-monotone-diffusion-flux]]. In addition to the strong state convergences in that lemma, the actual constitutive fields
$$q_h(t,x)=a(x,G_KU_h^n)\quad(t\in(t_{n-1},t_n],\ x\in K)$$
converge weakly in $L^{p'}(Q)$ to $a(x,\nabla u)$, and
$$\int_Qq_h\cdot G_h\overline U_h\longrightarrow\int_Qa(x,\nabla u)\cdot\nabla u,\qquad \sum_n\tau_n S_{h,p}(U_h^n)^p\longrightarrow0.$$
The final cell states converge strongly to $u(T)$ in $H$.

This includes convergence of a physical reconstruction of the actual numerical face fluxes. Let $r_{K,F}=x_F-x_K$, $s_{K,F}^n=\alpha_{0,K}|F|d_{K,F}^{1-p}\psi_p(\rho_{K,F}(U_h^n))$, $b_K^n=b_K(G_KU_h^n)$, and $c_K^n=|K|^{-1}\sum_Fs_{K,F}^nr_{K,F}$. On the physical pyramid $P_{K,F}$ with vertex $x_K$ and base $\overline F$ set
$$q_h^{\rm num}=b_K^n-c_K^n+\frac{s_{K,F}^n}{|F|}n_{K,F}.$$
Then $-|F|q_h^{\rm num}|_{P_{K,F}}\cdot n_{K,F}=Q_{K,F}^{\rm nl}(U_h^n)$ exactly, $q_h^{\rm num}-b_h\to0$ strongly in $L^{p'}(Q)$, with $b_h|_K=b_K^n$, and $q_h^{\rm num}\rightharpoonup a(x,\nabla u)$ in $L^{p'}(Q)$. No strong convergence of $G_h\overline U_h$ is inferred from mere monotonicity.

Finally the hypotheses of [[lem-mimetic-fv-parabolic-limit-identification]] can be supplied on this same subsequence by conforming limit recovery: take $w_h=u$ and $\widetilde q_h=a(x,\nabla w_h)=a(x,\nabla u)$. These are post-limit conforming functions, distinct from the computed companions $E_h\overline U_h$, constitutive fields $q_h$, and numerical fluxes $q_h^{\rm num}$. The computed convergence assertion above is established independently of this recovery observation.

title: Finite-volume diffusion on admissible meshes — Examples

items.title: Harmonic TPFA flux on a rectangular Voronoï mesh
items.statement: A two-cell rectangular Voronoï mesh reproduces the constant flux of the affine solution u(x,y)=x and conserves that flux across the shared face.
items.strategy: Compute cell and face centers, transmissibilities, and signed fluxes directly from the TPFA definition.

items.title: A nonorthogonal two-point flux gives a false transverse flux
items.statement: On two nonorthogonal cells, the Euclidean-distance TPFA formula applied to an affine state can return a nonzero flux when the exact normal diffusion flux is zero.
items.strategy: Give two explicit triangles sharing a vertical face and evaluate the naive two-point formula on u(x,y)=y.

items.title: Harmonic transmissibility across a one-dimensional material interface
items.statement: For two half-intervals with coefficients 1 and 9, the resistance-weighted harmonic transmissibility reproduces the exact stationary interface flux while the arithmetic average does not.
items.strategy: Solve the two-resistance continuous problem exactly and compare its interface flux with harmonic and arithmetic TPFA transmissibilities.

items.title: Affine anisotropic flux on a skew parallelogram
items.statement: The hybrid mimetic method reconstructs the exact gradient and all four integrated face fluxes for an affine state on a skew parallelogram with a full anisotropic tensor.
items.strategy: Evaluate the face means and integrated outward normals, then verify the reconstructed gradient and tensor-weighted fluxes.
